newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Oct crudes firm late upon nomination date.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Oct crudes firm late upon nomination date.

text.p: U.S. domestic crudes revived late Wednesday on refiner requirements ahead of the deadline for pipeline nominations, and with backwardation intact.
The Oct/Nov West Texas Intermediate roll eased only modestly into the nomination deadline, to 25 cents a barrel from hovering at 35-40 cents earlier Wednesday.
"There wasn't much of a play there. Refiners were pretty much balanced," a Texas trader said, noting that one refiner in particular, bought the spread and kept it steady.
October West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was at $24.55-65 a barrel, up five cents from the previous day.
Oct pipeline grades saw moderate dealings with small volumes traded over the session. WTI/Cushing Posting Plus moved between postings plus $2.00 to $2.10 a barrel.
Oct Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James traded between WTI minus 10 cents to plus eight cents, scaling back to positive territory in late action on short covering.
WTI/Midland stayed firm at WTI plus 10-12 cents, while West Texas Sour/Midland rose to WTI minus $1.00, up 20 cents.
Nov grades were barely talked but were underpinned by a closed import arbitrage, although upcoming autumn refinery turnarounds could crimp some demand, traders said.
"Refiners have little incentive to run that spot foreign barrel," another trader said, citing poor returns for gasoline in the U.S Gulf and the seasonal softening in margins.
